W2 (empirical), after E018. The tip is E017: 6.548 s, 0.7537, only about 0.07 pp above the 0.753 bar.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 rerun of E010: bit-identical. E013 LS 0.2: 0.7551. E014 Muon lr x1.5: 0.7557. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.578. E016 wd/2 0.7607/6.580. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only: 0.7502/5.99.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves about 4.8% time, roughly linear (E007 to E008). The epoch labels are probably off by about 0.5-1 (H4.2.3).
2. Compile saves about 4%.
3. EMA/Lookahead gives +0.97 pp for +0.06 s, the cheapest gain.
4. Muon gives +0.66 pp for +0.35 s.
5. Progressive resizing: time tracks pixel count. Dropping the 28 px phase (E018) saved 8.5% of time for -0.72 pp, about 0.085 pp per 1% of time. That is worse than the epoch dial (about 0.04 pp per 1%). Cutting low-resolution time costs more accuracy than cutting epochs.
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp (E010).
7. Resolution cliff: -14% time for -1.4 pp (E011). This is consistent with E018, so lower resolution is a bad trade at the margin.
8. LS, Muon lr and LR floor are flat within noise.
9. CUDA graphs and removing graph breaks give about 1% time each. The run is compute-bound.
10. Noise: a rerun of the same code is bit-identical, but a mathematically identical edit reshuffles the 3-seed mean by up to ±0.4 pp (E016 to E017 gave -0.7 pp). E016's wd gain was probably mostly noise. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and E016, and over-predicted E009, E011 and E018. Lesson: every cut in resolution or compute costs about 0.04-0.09 pp per 1% of time. With about 0.07 pp of margin, no trim is affordable. Accuracy-neutral knobs are unresolvable below about 0.4 pp.

Unsure: the true mean of the tip, probably about 0.755. Whether any free gain exists. The next step needs to be an accuracy gain, not a cut.

forecasts.reason: The dial costs about 0.35 pp per 1 epoch, and only 0.07 pp of margin is left, so it likely misses 0.753.
Narrowing group 2 saves time, but capacity loss at the 0.04-0.09 pp per 1% rate puts it under the bar.
Time is unchanged. A wd change is within the noise of about 0.4 pp, so a +0.2 pp gain cannot be resolved.
Removing a conv saves about 7% of time at a cost of about 0.5 pp, so it probably fails the bar.
A 20 px phase over 15% of steps saves about 3.5% of time; E011 and E018 say resolution cuts cost more than 0.25 pp, so it probably loses at least 0.3 pp.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 40-seed mean accuracy? If it is about 0.755 or higher, a half-epoch trim becomes affordable; if it is about 0.752, nothing is.
Is the E016 wd gain real? It was masked by an identical-math reshuffle of -0.7 pp in E017, so the true effect is unknown.
Is the time-versus-accuracy exchange rate from architecture cuts (width, depth, resolution) better than the epoch dial's 0.04 pp per 1% of time? E010, E011 and E018 suggest it is not.
